items.title: Mickey Roker interviewed by Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: And out of that come the blues singers like Dinah Washington and Sarah Vaughan. They come out of the churches, and Mahalia Jackson, you know, she was a spiritual singer, but if you listen to Aretha Franklin, you know what I’m saying? Ray Charles.

ctx.x: Give us an example. Give us an example.

I’m not too good at it, [humms]—I can’t really do it. But I know it when I hear it. But everything comes out of the church. Well you know the spiritual value of music is something that you must have. Spirit. That’s what the blues comes from, see, the Gospel. And the Negro spirituals in the corn field. Because see they took the drums away from us when we were slaves because we could communicate with each other. And they wanted to separate us, the slave masters. And when we was working on the plantation. So we…

Then you’ve got Charlie Parker, you’ve got Coleman Hawkins, they started swinging a little more and Ben Webster and Benny Carter, and it got more advanced with Dizzy Gillespie and Charlie Parker. See but it all come out of the fields. See it come out of them cotton fields, you know, with the Negro spiritual. It’s real sophisticated now. You go in the church and they’ve got drums and everything, bass you know? I mean dreadlocks. The Baptist churches, you go and look on the pulpit there’s a set of drums up there…
